title: A core gets the same number and description history entries
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test, with a description, description 1, and a Core Charge above $0, so it has a core described Core for followed by description 1.
  • Use a new part number, number 2, and a new description, description 2, that no part uses.
  • Start on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.
custom_steps:
1. Click the part A row.
  2. Replace the Part Number with number 2.
  3. Replace the Description with description 2.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Open the core's own Part History page.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens.

Step 2:

  • Part Number reads number 2.

Step 3:

  • Description reads description 2.

Step 4:

  • The save goes through.

Step 5:

  • The page is the core's own: its details name it Core for followed by description 2, with part number number 2.
  • Its newest entries are "Part number updated | Original number:" with part A's old number and "| New number:" number 2, and "Description updated | Original description: Core for" description 1 "| New description: Core for" description 2.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change), story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S10-R26: “When the part has a core, the core gets the same number or description entry. The core's description entries read its own description, "Core for {description}".”
  • S13-R15: “A changed description also renames the part's core, which reads "Core for {description}".”
  • S13-R18: “Saving a changed number renames the part in place. The part keeps its identity, its history, and every line that holds it. Its Part Library entry is renamed with it, and its core takes the same number. No new Part Library entry is created.”
  • S5-E3: “A core has no row of its own on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list, so it cannot be ticked for a bulk change. Its name (S13-R15) and its history show on the core's own Part History page. The core reason in S10-R13a applies when a core reaches a status change by any other route.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
